note: Recast from the revision by Constantino (1995), the original in English. The alate, the soldier and the large worker are described; the alate is described for the first time in that work. Soldier measurements: 5 soldiers from 5 colonies, head length 5.60—6.20 mm, maximum head width 5.60—6.10 mm, head height without the postmentum 3.05—3.50 mm, frontal tube length 0.13—0.22 mm, left mandible length 2.70—3.30 mm. The work designates a soldier neotype from Ulinquipata, Peru. S. chaquimayensis parvinasus Emerson 1945 was placed as a junior synonym of S. spinosus by that work.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate resembles S. dirus and S. spinosus but differs in the pilosity of the head capsule. The most similar soldier is S. spinosus, which is usually larger and has longer mandibles with larger teeth; the soldier of S. spinosus is, however, very variable and the two overlap in size. The distribution is a narrow strip from Colombia to Bolivia.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Eyes small, less than 1/4 of the head width without the eyes; ocelli small; fontanelle large and round. Antenna 20 segments. Anterior corners of the pronotum angled and with a sharp point; lateral margins nearly straight and narrowing backwards. Wings relatively short and dark; the ends of the media and cubitus distinct. Head capsule densely covered with numerous long hairs; postclypeus with about 16 hairs.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule short, length and width subequal, the sides narrowing forwards; posterior margin nearly round or weakly trilobed. Frontal tube prominent, the opening not visible in dorsal view. Labrum short, length and width subequal; lateral corners about right-angled; midlobe short. Antenna 19—20 segments. Postmentum not constricted, the posterior sides nearly parallel or slightly concave.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Large worker: head capsule with a few scattered erect setae; postclypeus with about 12 setae; fontanelle large and round. Antenna 19 or 20 segments. Thoracic spines well developed. Mandibles very similar to those of S. spinosus. The hindgut appears to be the same as in S. dirus, but the material is poorly preserved. Measurements (4 individuals from 4 colonies, mm): head length 2.60—2.85.
